sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports and module purpose
sections.what: Brings in the tools for building PowerPoint files and the project data types the replicator uses. The file header says it copies the layout of approved approach slides: timeline, governance, module and workstream slides.
sections.why: Needed so the rest of the file can build slides, tables, colors and shapes.
sections.watch_out: The math library is imported inside the functions that need it, not at the top, so any new function that uses math must import it too.

sections.name: ApproachSlideReplicator (part 1)
sections.title: Starting the deck from the template
sections.what: Starts a new blank presentation sized to the template. Then it adds the slides in a fixed order: title, workstream overview, timeline, governance, and one module slide per workstream that has modules. Each slide is added only when its matching template exists.
sections.why: Each slide type is optional, so the app can still produce a deck when a past proposal lacked that slide style.
sections.watch_out: The template's size entry must include width, height, ratio and a 16:9 flag, or the build fails before any slide is made.

sections.name: ApproachSlideReplicator (part 2)
sections.title: Module slides and the summary count
sections.what: Adds one module detail slide for each workstream that has modules. Then it prints a summary of the slides and returns the deck. The printed list is fixed text, so it shows the same items even when some slide types were skipped.
sections.why: Gives the user progress messages while the build runs.
sections.watch_out: Because the printed list is fixed, it can say a slide was created when it was actually skipped.

sections.name: ApproachSlideReplicator (part 3)
sections.title: Title, project name and workstream overview
sections.what: Adds the project name under the title. Then it builds the workstream overview slide: one text box per workstream showing its name, duration in weeks and module count, stacked down the slide. The title color comes from the template, with black as the fallback.
sections.why: The overview gives a high-level view of the approach before the detail slides. The code comments say this layout is a simple placeholder that will later copy the template exactly.
sections.watch_out: Boxes are placed one inch apart with no limit, so many workstreams will run off the bottom of the slide.

sections.name: ApproachSlideReplicator: _create_timeline_slide
sections.title: Choosing how to draw the timeline
sections.what: Creates a slide titled Project Timeline. It reads the timeline style from the template, using a table by default, and passes the work to the matching drawing routine.
sections.why: Past proposals used different timeline styles, so the code copies whichever style the template names.
sections.watch_out: Any style other than table or chart is drawn as bars, so an unexpected style value is handled without any warning.

sections.name: ApproachSlideReplicator (part 5)
sections.title: Week table and bar chart drawing
sections.what: Draws the table version: one row per workstream, one column per week, with active weeks shaded green. Also draws the bar version, where each workstream is a labeled blue bar placed by its start week and length.
sections.why: The two styles need different drawing approaches, so each has its own routine.
sections.watch_out: The table is capped at 15 columns, so timelines longer than about 13 weeks are cut off with no warning.

sections.name: ApproachSlideReplicator (part 6)
sections.title: Bar labels, chart fallback and governance slide
sections.what: Writes each bar's duration label, such as 4w. The chart style simply draws bars, because a real editable chart is not built yet. Then builds the Governance and Meeting Cadence slide, with lines for the steering committee, working team and key workshops, each shown only when there is data for it.
sections.why: The chart fallback reason is stated in the code: a real chart needs extra data that is not written yet. Hiding empty lines keeps the slide clean when a proposal has little governance data.
sections.watch_out: Users who expect an editable chart will get drawn bars instead, and the steering committee wording is a rough guess.

sections.name: ApproachSlideReplicator: _extract_governance_info
sections.title: Collecting governance details and starting module slides
sections.what: Scans every module for governance notes and collects three things: the steering committee frequency, whether weekly syncs exist, and the list of workshops. Then starts the module slide for one workstream, titled with its name and Modules and Activities, and creates an empty table sized from the template.
sections.why: Likely reason: governance notes are stored on each module, so they are gathered from the modules.
sections.watch_out: Each later module overwrites the steering committee value, and workshop names can repeat. The column count comes from the template and defaults to four.

sections.name: ApproachSlideReplicator (part 8)
sections.title: Filling the module table and slide titles
sections.what: Fills the module table with a header row of Module, Duration, Key Activities and Deliverables, then one row per module. Each row shows the module name, its duration, up to three activities with a count of the rest, and up to three deliverables. It also defines the helper that adds a title to any slide.
sections.why: Keeps each row short enough to fit on the slide.
sections.watch_out: Writes to the third and fourth columns without checking how many columns exist, so a template with fewer than four columns that has deliverables will crash.

sections.name: ApproachSlideReplicator: export
sections.title: Saving the deck to a file
sections.what: Saves the finished deck to a file in the output exports folder, using the given name or Approach_Section.pptx by default. Returns the full path of the saved file.
sections.why: Gives the user a file they can open, and returns the path so other code can use it.
sections.watch_out: It raises an error if called before the deck is built, and it overwrites any existing file with the same name without asking.

sections.name: create_approach_presentation
sections.title: One-step convenience function
sections.what: Builds the replicator, creates the deck, saves it and returns the file path, all in one call.
sections.why: Lets other code produce the approach deck with a single call.
sections.watch_out: The output folder is fixed to the default, so there is no way to choose a different folder through this function.

summary: Builds a new PowerPoint deck for the approach section of a proposal, copying the layout and styling of the analyzed template slides and filling them with the project's workstreams, timeline, governance and modules.
purpose: Turns the generated project plan into PowerPoint slides that look like the firm's existing proposals, so the output can be used without manual reformatting.
why: Likely reason: the analyzer extracts real layout details from past proposals, and this module applies them, so new decks match the house style.
how: First the caller passes in the template and project. A blank deck is sized to the template. Then a title slide, workstream overview, timeline, governance slide and one module table per workstream are added in that order, each only if its template exists. The finished deck is saved to the output exports folder.
inputs: A template dictionary from the approach analyzer, containing slide sizes and style details for each slide type. A ProjectStructure holding the project name, workstreams and their modules, activities and governance notes. An optional file name and output folder.
outputs: A PowerPoint file named Approach_Section.pptx by default, saved in output/exports, and the path to that file is returned. Console messages report progress when verbose is on.
risks: Module tables assume four columns and write to the third and fourth columns without checking. The workstream overview boxes can run off the bottom of the slide. Existing files with the same name are overwritten without warning.
debug: Start with the template: if a slide is missing, its template key is probably None or empty. For a crash in the module table, check the template's table column count. For a wrong timeline, check the template's visualization type. Confirm the output folder exists and that the file is not open in PowerPoint.
